Name: Oil Change
ShortDescription: Replace engine oil and filter to keep your engine running clean and cool.
DetailedDescription: Engine oil lubricates all moving metal parts, reduces friction, absorbs heat, and carries away contaminants. Over time, oil breaks down, becomes acidic, and loses viscosity — leading to sludge and accelerated wear. Modern full-synthetic oils last 7,500–10,000 miles; conventional 3,000–5,000 miles.
WhyItMatters: Skipping oil changes is the #1 cause of premature engine failure. A fresh oil change costs $60–$100; an engine replacement costs $4,000–$10,000+.
Interval: Every 5,000–7,500 mi (full synthetic) or 3,000–5,000 mi (conventional)
SkipConsequence: Oil sludge, increased engine wear, potential engine seizure.

Name: Transmission Fluid Service
ShortDescription: Drain and replace the fluid that keeps your transmission shifting smoothly.
DetailedDescription: Transmission fluid lubricates gears, clutches, and seals. It also acts as hydraulic fluid in automatic transmissions. Degraded fluid loses viscosity and can cause harsh shifting, slipping, and overheating. Most manufacturers recommend service every 30,000–60,000 miles.
WhyItMatters: Transmission replacement averages $3,000–$7,000. A fluid service at $150–$250 can prevent that.
Interval: Every 30,000–60,000 miles or per manufacturer recommendation
SkipConsequence: Harsh or delayed shifting, overheating transmission, premature clutch pack failure.

Name: Coolant / Antifreeze Flush
ShortDescription: Replace the coolant that prevents your engine from overheating or freezing.
DetailedDescription: Coolant (antifreeze) regulates engine temperature and prevents corrosion inside the cooling system. Over time, pH drops, corrosion inhibitors deplete, and water pump seals can be damaged. Old coolant can cause scaling and blockages in the radiator.
WhyItMatters: Overheating is a top cause of catastrophic engine damage. A head gasket failure alone runs $1,500–$4,000.
Interval: Every 30,000 miles or every 2–5 years depending on coolant type
SkipConsequence: Corrosion in cooling system, thermostat failure, water pump damage, overheating.

Name: Brake Fluid Exchange
ShortDescription: Replace the hydraulic fluid that activates your brakes every time you press the pedal.
DetailedDescription: Brake fluid is hygroscopic — it absorbs water from the atmosphere over time. As water content rises, the fluid's boiling point drops (vapor lock risk) and it promotes internal corrosion of calipers, lines, and the ABS modulator. DOT 3/4 should be replaced every 2 years or 30,000 miles.
WhyItMatters: Vapor lock under heavy braking can cause complete brake failure. ABS modulator replacement costs $500–$1,500.
Interval: Every 2 years or 30,000 miles
SkipConsequence: Spongy brake pedal, vapor lock, internal corrosion, brake failure risk.

Name: Power Steering Fluid Service
ShortDescription: Flush the fluid that makes steering effortless.
DetailedDescription: Hydraulic power steering systems rely on clean fluid to transmit force. Contaminated fluid can damage the power steering pump and rack seals, leading to leaks and hard steering. Electric power steering (EPS) vehicles do not require this service.
WhyItMatters: Power steering pump replacement: $200–$600. Rack & pinion: $1,000–$2,500.
Interval: Every 30,000–50,000 miles or if fluid appears dark/gritty
SkipConsequence: Noisy pump, hard steering, seal degradation, pump failure.

Name: Differential Fluid Service
ShortDescription: Replace the gear oil that lubricates front and rear differentials.
DetailedDescription: The differential allows wheels to rotate at different speeds when cornering. Differential fluid lubricates ring-and-pinion gears and bearings. On AWD/4WD vehicles, both front and rear differentials and the transfer case need periodic fluid changes. Neglected differentials whine loudly before failing.
WhyItMatters: Differential replacement: $1,500–$4,000. Fluid service: $80–$150 per axle.
Interval: Every 30,000–50,000 miles (check manufacturer spec)
SkipConsequence: Gear whine, bearing damage, differential failure, loss of AWD function.

Name: Brake Pad Replacement
ShortDescription: Replace worn brake pads before they damage your rotors and compromise stopping power.
DetailedDescription: Brake pads press against rotors to create friction and slow the vehicle. Most pads have wear indicators that squeal when they reach ~3mm. Once metal-on-metal contact occurs, rotors are scored and must be replaced too, dramatically increasing repair cost.
WhyItMatters: Pads alone: $150–$300/axle. Waiting until metal-on-metal: add $200–$400 for rotors. More critically — stopping distance increases significantly.
Interval: Every 25,000–70,000 miles depending on driving style
SkipConsequence: Reduced stopping power, rotor damage, safety risk.

Name: Brake Rotor Replacement
ShortDescription: Replace warped or worn rotors to eliminate vibration and restore braking performance.
DetailedDescription: Rotors can warp from heat cycles or become too thin to safely resurface. Warped rotors cause pedal pulsation and vibration during braking. Modern thin-cast rotors are typically replaced rather than resurfaced.
WhyItMatters: Pulsating brake pedal indicates compromised stopping ability. Warped rotors extend stopping distances.
Interval: Every 50,000–70,000 miles or when thickness falls below minimum spec
SkipConsequence: Vibration, longer stopping distance, caliper damage.

Name: Brake Caliper Service / Replacement
ShortDescription: Service or replace the hydraulic clamps that squeeze your brake pads against the rotors.
DetailedDescription: Calipers are hydraulic pistons that push brake pads against rotors when you press the brake pedal. They can seize in the applied position (causing constant drag and overheating) or fail to engage fully. A seized caliper causes uneven braking, rapid pad wear on one side, and a pulling sensation.
WhyItMatters: A seized caliper can wear through pads in 5,000 miles and destroy a rotor in days.
Interval: Inspect every 30,000 miles; replace when seized or leaking
SkipConsequence: Vehicle pulling, rapid uneven wear, potential brake failure, overheated rotor.

Name: Tire Rotation
ShortDescription: Move tires to different positions so they wear evenly and last longer.
DetailedDescription: Front tires wear faster due to steering forces. Rotating tires every 5,000–7,500 miles equalizes tread wear across all four tires, extending tire life by up to 50% and maintaining balanced handling.
WhyItMatters: Skipping rotation can halve tire life. A set of tires costs $400–$1,200. Rotation is $20–$50.
Interval: Every 5,000–7,500 miles (align with oil changes)
SkipConsequence: Uneven tread wear, premature tire replacement, handling imbalance.

Name: Wheel Alignment
ShortDescription: Adjust wheel angles so your car drives straight and tires wear evenly.
DetailedDescription: Alignment adjusts camber, caster, and toe angles to manufacturer specs. Misalignment from potholes, curb strikes, or worn suspension components causes rapid tire wear on one edge and can pull the vehicle to one side.
WhyItMatters: Misalignment can destroy a set of new tires in 10,000 miles. Alignment service is $80–$130.
Interval: Every 12,000 miles or after suspension work / tire purchase
SkipConsequence: Rapid edge wear on tires, pulling/drifting, premature tire failure.

Name: Tire Balancing
ShortDescription: Balance weights on wheels to eliminate vibration at highway speeds.
DetailedDescription: Unbalanced tires cause vibration felt through the steering wheel or seat at certain speeds. Over time this vibration accelerates wear on wheel bearings and suspension components.
WhyItMatters: Wheel bearing replacement: $250–$500. Balancing: $15–$25 per tire.
Interval: Every 12,000 miles or when vibration is noticed
SkipConsequence: Vibration, uneven tread wear, bearing and suspension wear.

Name: TPMS Sensor Service
ShortDescription: Service or replace tire pressure monitoring sensors that keep your warning light off.
DetailedDescription: TPMS sensors are battery-powered devices inside each wheel. Batteries last 7–10 years. After a tire change, sensors must be relearned to the vehicle's computer. A failed sensor triggers a dashboard warning light and means the system is no longer monitoring pressure — a safety concern.
WhyItMatters: Under-inflated tires reduce fuel economy by up to 3% and increase blowout risk. A failed sensor gives false confidence.
Interval: Replace batteries at 7–10 years; relearn after every tire service
SkipConsequence: Persistent warning light, no pressure monitoring, potential undetected underinflation.

Name: Cabin Air Filter
ShortDescription: Replace the filter that cleans the air you breathe inside the cabin.
DetailedDescription: The cabin air filter traps dust, pollen, mold spores, and pollutants before they enter the passenger compartment through the HVAC system. A clogged filter reduces airflow, strains the blower motor, and allows allergens through.
WhyItMatters: Air quality directly affects driver alertness and passenger health. Blower motor replacement: $200–$400.
Interval: Every 15,000–25,000 miles or 1 year
SkipConsequence: Poor cabin air quality, reduced A/C and heat performance, blower motor strain.

Name: Engine Air Filter
ShortDescription: Replace the filter protecting your engine from dirt and debris.
DetailedDescription: The engine air filter prevents abrasive particles from entering the intake and causing cylinder wall wear. A restricted filter leans out the air/fuel mixture, reduces power, and increases fuel consumption.
WhyItMatters: A dirty filter can reduce fuel economy by up to 10%. Replacing it costs $20–$50 and takes minutes.
Interval: Every 15,000–30,000 miles
SkipConsequence: Reduced power, poor fuel economy, potential engine contamination.

Name: Fuel Filter Replacement
ShortDescription: Replace the filter that keeps debris out of your fuel injectors and pump.
DetailedDescription: The fuel filter screens contaminants from gasoline before it reaches the fuel injectors and pump. A clogged filter starves the engine under load, causing hesitation, rough idle, and can burn out the fuel pump by making it work against increased restriction.
WhyItMatters: Fuel pump replacement: $400–$900. Fuel filter: $30–$80.
Interval: Every 20,000–40,000 miles (varies widely by vehicle)
SkipConsequence: Engine hesitation, hard starting, fuel pump failure.

Name: Battery Test & Replacement
ShortDescription: Test your battery's health and replace it before it leaves you stranded.
DetailedDescription: Lead-acid batteries degrade over 3–5 years. Cold cranking amps (CCA) drop with age, making cold starts difficult. A bad battery can also damage the alternator as it works harder to compensate. Battery tests take 5 minutes with a conductance tester.
WhyItMatters: Being stranded costs time and potentially a tow ($100–$200). Alternator damage adds $300–$700.
Interval: Test every year after 3 years; replace every 3–5 years
SkipConsequence: No-start condition, stranded vehicle, potential alternator damage.

Name: Spark Plug Replacement
ShortDescription: Replace worn spark plugs to restore engine performance and fuel economy.
DetailedDescription: Spark plugs ignite the air/fuel mixture in each cylinder. Worn plugs misfire, reducing power, increasing fuel consumption, and potentially damaging the catalytic converter ($800–$2,500) from unburned fuel passing through.
WhyItMatters: A catalytic converter damaged by misfires costs many times more than a plug service.
Interval: Every 30,000 miles (copper/platinum) or 60,000–100,000 miles (iridium)
SkipConsequence: Misfires, rough idle, poor fuel economy, catalytic converter damage.

Name: Alternator Test & Replacement
ShortDescription: Test the alternator that charges your battery while the engine runs.
DetailedDescription: The alternator converts engine rotation into electrical current, keeping the battery charged and powering all electrical systems. A failing alternator causes the battery to drain while driving, dimming lights, and flickering gauges. Once the battery is depleted, the vehicle stalls.
WhyItMatters: A failed alternator strands you even with a healthy battery. Replacement: $350–$800.
Interval: Test at any no-start or electrical complaint; typical lifespan 80,000–150,000 miles
SkipConsequence: Battery drain, vehicle stall, stranded — even on the highway.

Name: Serpentine Belt Replacement
ShortDescription: Replace the belt driving your alternator, power steering pump, and A/C compressor.
DetailedDescription: The serpentine belt drives multiple accessories — alternator, power steering pump (if hydraulic), A/C compressor, and water pump on many vehicles. A broken belt disables all of these simultaneously and strands the vehicle. Belts crack and glaze with age and heat exposure.
WhyItMatters: A snapped serpentine belt disables charging, cooling, and steering simultaneously. Belt: $100–$200. Tow + emergency repair: $300+.
Interval: Every 60,000–100,000 miles or at first sign of cracking/glazing
SkipConsequence: Sudden loss of charging, A/C, and power steering; overheating; stranded vehicle.

Name: Shocks & Struts Replacement
ShortDescription: Replace worn shocks or struts to restore ride comfort and vehicle control.
DetailedDescription: Shocks and struts dampen road vibration and keep tires in contact with the road. Worn units cause excessive body roll, nose-dive under braking, bounce over bumps, and increased stopping distance. The 'bounce test' (push down on a corner — if it bounces more than once, shocks are likely worn).
WhyItMatters: Worn struts increase stopping distance by up to 20% and accelerate tire and suspension wear.
Interval: Every 50,000–100,000 miles or when bounce/handling issues appear
SkipConsequence: Poor handling, increased stopping distance, tire cupping, unsafe control.

Name: Ball Joint Replacement
ShortDescription: Replace worn ball joints — the pivot points connecting your wheels to the suspension.
DetailedDescription: Ball joints are spherical bearings that allow the suspension to move up and down while the wheel steers. Worn ball joints have play that causes clunking over bumps, tire wear, and imprecise steering. A completely failed ball joint causes the wheel to collapse outward — an extremely dangerous situation.
WhyItMatters: A separated ball joint causes immediate loss of steering control and vehicle collapse. This is one of the few maintenance failures that can cause a crash at any speed.
Interval: Inspect every 30,000 miles; replace when play is detected
SkipConsequence: Clunking, imprecise steering, tire wear, risk of wheel separation and crash.

Name: CV Axle / Boot Replacement
ShortDescription: Replace torn CV boots or worn CV axles that transmit power to your front wheels.
DetailedDescription: Constant velocity (CV) axles transmit engine torque to the front wheels on FWD/AWD vehicles while allowing suspension travel. The rubber CV boots protect the joint's grease. A torn boot lets grease escape and moisture in — quickly destroying the joint. Clicking during turns is the classic symptom of a worn joint.
WhyItMatters: CV boot replacement: $150–$250. Full CV axle: $250–$500. Ignoring a torn boot: $500+ in axle damage.
Interval: Inspect at every oil change; replace boot immediately when torn
SkipConsequence: Clicking during turns, joint failure, loss of power to wheel, drivability loss.

Name: Tie Rod End Replacement
ShortDescription: Replace worn tie rod ends that link your steering rack to your wheel hubs.
DetailedDescription: Tie rod ends are the link between the steering rack and wheel knuckles. Worn ends have rotational play that causes imprecise steering, wandering, and uneven tire wear. They're detectable by grabbing the tire at 9 and 3 o'clock and feeling for play. Always requires realignment after replacement.
WhyItMatters: A failed tie rod end causes sudden loss of steering. Always requires wheel alignment afterward.
Interval: Inspect every 30,000 miles; replace when play is detected
SkipConsequence: Steering wander, uneven tire wear, potential loss of directional control.

Name: 30,000-Mile Service
ShortDescription: Comprehensive inspection and fluid/filter service at the 30K milestone.
DetailedDescription: Typically includes: engine air filter, cabin air filter, spark plugs (if due), tire rotation, brake inspection, fluid level top-offs, multi-point vehicle inspection, and transmission fluid service. Catches developing issues before they become expensive repairs.
WhyItMatters: Milestone services maintain manufacturer warranty compliance and catch ~70% of developing issues early.
Interval: At 30,000-mile odometer milestone
SkipConsequence: Missed wear items, potential warranty concerns, compounding maintenance debt.

Name: 60,000-Mile Service
ShortDescription: Major milestone service covering all wear items at the 60K mark.
DetailedDescription: Includes all 30K service items plus: timing belt inspection (if applicable), coolant flush, brake fluid exchange, fuel system cleaning, serpentine belt inspection, and full suspension/steering check.
WhyItMatters: The 60K service is the most important milestone — many systems hit wear thresholds simultaneously.
Interval: At 60,000-mile odometer milestone
SkipConsequence: Multiple deferred maintenance items compounding into expensive failures.

Name: Timing Belt Replacement
ShortDescription: Replace the belt that synchronizes your engine's valves and pistons — before it snaps.
DetailedDescription: Interference engines (most modern engines) will suffer catastrophic valve/piston collision if the timing belt breaks. The belt shows no external warning before failure. Water pump is typically replaced at the same time since it shares the belt path.
WhyItMatters: A snapped timing belt = bent valves, damaged pistons = $3,000–$10,000 engine repair or replacement. Belt + water pump service: $500–$1,200.
Interval: Every 60,000–105,000 miles per manufacturer spec
SkipConsequence: Catastrophic engine destruction if belt snaps on an interference engine.

Name: Fuel Injection / Induction Cleaning
ShortDescription: Clean carbon deposits from fuel injectors, intake valves, and throttle body.
DetailedDescription: Over time, carbon deposits accumulate on fuel injectors, intake valves (especially on GDI engines with no port washing), and throttle bodies. This causes rough idle, hesitation, and reduced fuel economy. Professional cleaning restores atomization and airflow.
WhyItMatters: Carbon buildup is especially severe on GDI engines. Walnut blasting for GDI intake valves: $400–$700. Regular induction service prevents it.
Interval: Every 30,000–45,000 miles or at idle/hesitation complaints
SkipConsequence: Rough idle, hesitation, reduced MPG, potential misfires.

Name: Wheel Bearing Replacement
ShortDescription: Replace a worn wheel bearing causing humming or grinding at highway speed.
DetailedDescription: Wheel bearings allow wheels to spin freely with minimal friction. A worn bearing produces a distinctive humming or grinding noise that changes pitch with speed and worsens in turns. Failure causes the wheel to wobble and can ultimately seize or separate from the vehicle.
WhyItMatters: A seized wheel bearing can cause the wheel to lock or separate. Early replacement: $250–$500. Ignored until complete failure: $500–$900 plus potential crash risk.
Interval: Replace when noise or play is detected; typical lifespan 85,000–100,000 miles
SkipConsequence: Progressive hub damage, wheel wobble, risk of wheel lockup or separation.

Name: A/C System Service
ShortDescription: Inspect, recharge, or repair the air conditioning system.
DetailedDescription: A/C systems use refrigerant (R-134a or R-1234yf) under pressure to cool cabin air. Low refrigerant means inadequate cooling. Leaks must be identified and sealed before recharging. Compressor, condenser, and evaporator can all fail. Georgia summers make this a priority.
WhyItMatters: A/C compressor replacement: $800–$1,500. A recharge to catch a small leak early: $150–$250.
Interval: Service when cooling is inadequate; recharge every 3–5 years if system is leak-free
SkipConsequence: No cabin cooling, compressor damage from oil-depleted refrigerant, passenger discomfort.

Name: Heater Core Service
ShortDescription: Service the small radiator inside your dashboard that provides cabin heat.
DetailedDescription: The heater core is a small heat exchanger that circulates hot coolant through the dashboard to warm the cabin. Leaks cause fog on the inside of the windshield, a sweet smell, and wet carpet. A clogged core produces inadequate heat. It's one of the more labor-intensive repairs due to dashboard removal.
WhyItMatters: A leaking heater core dumps coolant inside the cabin and can cause overheating. Repair: $600–$1,200 due to labor.
Interval: Service when fog, sweet smell, or no heat is present; flush preventively every 60,000 miles
SkipConsequence: Windshield fogging, coolant loss, overheating, wet carpet damage.

Name: Thermostat Replacement
ShortDescription: Replace the valve that regulates coolant flow and engine operating temperature.
DetailedDescription: The thermostat is a wax-pellet valve that opens when the engine reaches operating temperature, allowing coolant to flow to the radiator. A stuck-open thermostat causes the engine to run cold (poor fuel economy, heater performance). A stuck-closed thermostat causes overheating.
WhyItMatters: A stuck-closed thermostat leads directly to overheating and potential head gasket failure ($1,500–$4,000). Thermostat: $100–$250.
Interval: Replace at first sign of temperature irregularity or every 60,000 miles preventively
SkipConsequence: Overheating (closed) or running cold and poor heat/economy (open).

Name: Wiper Blade Replacement
ShortDescription: Replace worn wiper blades that streak or chatter for clear visibility in rain.
DetailedDescription: Wiper blades are made of rubber that degrades from UV exposure, heat, and oxidation. Streaking, chattering, or skipping are all signs of worn blades. In Georgia's heavy summer rain and occasional ice, clear wipers are a safety-critical item.
WhyItMatters: Visibility is a primary crash prevention factor. New wipers: $30–$60. Vision impaired by bad wipers in a downpour: priceless.
Interval: Every 6–12 months or at first sign of streaking
SkipConsequence: Reduced visibility in rain, scratch risk to windshield if rubber separates.

Name: Headlight Restoration / Bulb Replacement
ShortDescription: Restore cloudy headlight lenses or replace bulbs for maximum nighttime visibility.
DetailedDescription: Polycarbonate headlight lenses oxidize and yellow over time, diffusing and reducing light output by up to 80%. Restoration removes oxidation and applies UV coating. Single burned-out bulbs reduce visibility by 50%; burned-out bulbs are also a ticketable offense in Georgia.
WhyItMatters: AAA studies show oxidized headlights reduce visibility to levels below legal minimums. Restoration: $50–$100. New assembly if too far gone: $200–$600.
Interval: Restore at first sign of yellowing; replace bulbs immediately when burned out
SkipConsequence: Severely reduced night visibility, legal liability, difficulty seeing pedestrians and obstacles.
